dir accepts an absolute directory path or a path relative to the user home directory. Thumbnails are saved in a thumbnails subdirectory with tn_ prepended to filenames. The documented height and width percentages are 1 through 99; the client forwards integers without adding range validation.

The result is a list with optional failed, file, reason and thumbnail_file fields. failed is documented as the integer 1, returned only when a thumbnail was not created; the existing integer policy does not enforce that singleton enum. reason is failure information and file and thumbnail_file are absolute paths. API status 1 does not establish that every thumbnail was created; inspect each row. Status 1 accepts empty lists. Reviewed all-failed batches report status 0 with row reasons: valid nonempty row lists are returned in full. Status 0 with no rows raises ApiErrorException; an empty directory can have errors() empty because upstream errors is null. Missing data, malformed roots or known row fields remain payload mismatches with outcomeConfirmed=false; integer status validation and outer WHM failure precedence remain strict.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 82 and later; disabled when the WebServer role is disabled. Paths are account-server paths forwarded unchanged, without local filesystem access, path normalization or resolution.

image_file and save_original_as accept absolute paths or paths relative to the user home directory. Height and width are documented as positive pixel dimensions; the client forwards integers without adding range validation. The result is the absolute resized image path as a string.

Omitting saveOriginalAs (including null) omits save_original_as and the server does not save a copy of the original. Explicit empty string is sent unchanged. saveOriginalAs must name a NEW FILE path: an existing path, including a directory, is rejected by the server. The pinned parameter prose says directory, but reviewed _get_safe_image_file source and both-route cPanel 11.138.0.19 behavior resolve it to a new file path: img/orig.png retained the original 10x5 image, while existing directory img was rejected. No local filesystem check is performed.

Changes account image files through form POST. The pinned source labels rollback clean but defines no client restore protocol. The client makes one attempt with no automatic retry, restore, cleanup, backup, collision handling or atomicity guarantee, and performs no automatic rollback.
